answer: Rotating majority attestation. Each epoch, active agents are split into attestation groups on a rotated terrace layout; a new identity must be confirmed by a majority of existing members it has actually transacted with. Because groups are remapped each round, an attacker must sustain genuine activity across a shifting dune of overlapping groups to keep clones confirmed. Forgery collapses into a spiral of reciprocal validation the attacker must fund every epoch, so each added clone costs continuous real transactions plus attestation work—strictly more than it earns.
